name: Suriname
headline: Since May 2025 the Civil Code gives Surinamese patients a right to a copy of their file, but no data protection law or regulator exists.

access.summary: Article 7:456 of the Civil Code, in force since 1 May 2025, gives a right to inspect and copy the medical file, with no fixed deadline and a fee allowed for copies. The My Health app shows part of the record for patients of about 63 listed GPs.
detail: Article 456 of Book 7 says the care provider gives the patient, on request and as soon as possible, inspection of and a copy of the file. The provider may charge a reasonable fee for the copy. Information that would harm another person's privacy is held back.

The new Civil Code took effect on 1 May 2025 after the President decided against requests for delay. A doctor writing in Starnieuws in September 2026 said patients now have a direct legal right to read and copy what the doctor wrote.

The Ministry of Health launched the My Health app in May 2025. It shows medical advice, vital signs and diagnoses from certified GP record systems. Patients activate it with a QR code from their own GP.

The Ministry's list of activation sites names 63 doctors in the Paramaribo region, plus a Nickerie list of 10 that repeats names from it. No user figure was found. Under the access rules this is base 45, minus 5 for the fee and 5 for no fixed deadline, plus 5 for an officially documented portal.

sources.title: Burgerlijk Wetboek Boek 7 (S.B. 2024 no. 164), De Nationale Assemblee

control.summary: The Civil Code bars providers from sharing the file outside the treating team without consent, and patients can demand its destruction. With no opt-out from sharing and no patient access log, this sits at the top of the 20 to 35 band, like NRU and MCO.
detail: Article 457 of Book 7 says the provider must not give information or copies to others without the patient's consent. People directly involved in the treatment, and a stand-in for the provider, are not counted as others.
Article 455 lets a patient ask for the file to be destroyed. The provider must do so within three months, unless keeping it matters greatly to someone else or a law requires it.

In the My Health app the GP issues the activation code and so decides which data reach which patient, the Ministry says. No way for patients to see who opened their record, or to set sharing choices, was found.

sources.title: Burgerlijk Wetboek Boek 7 (S.B. 2024 no. 164), De Nationale Assemblee

privacy.summary: Suriname has no data protection law in force and no data protection authority, so this sits below the 45 to 66 general-law band. A bill with health data as a special category, 72-hour breach notice and a Commissioner is still pending before the National Assembly.
detail: Article 17 of the Constitution gives everyone a right to respect for private life, home, honour and good name. No general statute applies it to personal data.

The draft Wet Bescherming Privacy en Persoonsgegevens bans processing of health data except on listed grounds, such as care. It requires breach notice to an independent Commissioner within 72 hours where possible. The National Assembly lists it as under consideration.

The draft caps fines at SRD 10,000 or 4% of worldwide turnover, whichever is higher. No health data breach in Suriname was found in the review period. The Civil Code's confidentiality rule is the only health-specific privacy duty in force.

commercial.summary: The only rule in force is the Civil Code's ban on providers releasing file contents without consent. No law covers health apps, data brokers, marketing or sales of de-identified data, and the pending privacy bill's marketing objection right is not law.
detail: Article 457 of Book 7 stops a care provider from passing information or copies of the file to others without the patient's consent. It binds providers under a treatment contract, not app makers or brokers.
The draft privacy bill would let a person object to direct marketing, including profiling, after which the data may no longer be used for it. It would treat health data as a special category.
Neither rule reaches consumer health apps today. No rules on selling health data or de-identified data were found.

journey.summary: Certified EHRs run at the state primary care service RGD and some private GPs, and Suriname passed HL7 FHIR tests for e-prescriptions in 2026. In November 2025 the health minister said little had been achieved in three years and ended the IS4H consultant's contract.
detail: The 2022 digital health agenda says about 90% of people live on the coast, served by private GPs or the RGD, which ran 43 clinics. It planned a health information exchange and EHRs in more facilities.

Two EHR products, from Health E Solutions and Weblocher, are certified. The digital death certificate has been in use since January 2025. In August 2026 the Ministry won a regional award for rolling out the EHR at the RGD, with all staff trained, and said rollout at the Medical Mission was being prepared.
Suriname completed all tracks at the 2026 PH4H Connectathon, including patient summaries, vaccine certificates and e-prescriptions. That was a test, not live national exchange.
No hospital, lab, pharmacy or insurer link was found. Suriname is outside the EU, so the European Health Data Space does not apply.

clinical.summary: Clinicians see one record only inside a single network, such as the RGD's EHR. No exchange that lets a hospital doctor open a GP or RGD record was found.
detail: The Ministry says the EHR at the RGD is in use and that the Medical Mission, which serves the interior, is preparing to adopt it.
The 2022 agenda planned a health information exchange so clinical systems could share data. The minister's November 2025 statement that little had been achieved suggests this was not in place.
The Civil Code lets the treating team see the file without extra consent. No emergency access rule or national record for clinicians was found.

research.summary: Article 7:458 lets providers release patient data for public health research without consent only when asking is impractical, and only if the patient has not objected. Counting that partial objection route and the Ministry's research ethics committee, this is 40 plus 3 plus 3.
detail: Release without consent needs a public interest, data the study cannot do without, and either safeguards for privacy or data that cannot be traced to a person. The release must be noted in the file.
The Commissie Mensgebonden Wetenschappelijk Onderzoek was installed in May 2020 to help the Director of Health screen clinical and scientific studies. Its current work and caseload were not checked.
The draft privacy bill would treat research as a compatible purpose. No public register of data uses was found.

sources.title: Burgerlijk Wetboek Boek 7 (S.B. 2024 no. 164), De Nationale Assemblee
Commissie mensgebonden Wetenschappelijk onderzoek geinstalleerd (STVS)

ai.summary: No law, guidance or device route for clinical AI was found, and the Registration Commission assesses medicines only. Suriname began UNESCO's AI readiness assessment in August 2026, a diagnostic, not a rule.
detail: The Ministry of Health's Registration Commission assesses and registers packaged medicines. No rule for software or AI as a medical device was found.
On 27 August 2026 Suriname held the opening stakeholder meeting for UNESCO's RAM 2.0 AI readiness assessment, the first in the English- and Dutch-speaking Caribbean. It is an assessment, not a rule.
The draft privacy bill would give a right not to be subject to solely automated decisions with legal or similar effects. It is not in force.
